title: WPMS/83/1994 of USHA BREECO LIMITED Vs COMMISSION OF ENTERTAINMENT TAX

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(1) Writ Petition No. 1031 (M/S) of 2007
(Old No. 1044/1997)
 1- Usha Breco Limited, Chandi Devo Rope Way,
 Near Gauri Shankar Temple, Hardwar,
 through its Divisional Manager, Sri M.J. Raghuram,
 2- Sri K.P. Pandey S/o Sri Ram Kishore Pandey,
 R/o Haridwar, a shareholder of Usha Breco Ltd. - Petitioners
 Versus
1. State of U.P. through its Chief Secretary,
State Secretariat, Vidhan Sabha Marg, Lucknow.
2. Commissioner of Entertainment Tax, U.P.
Jawahar Bhawan, Ashok Road, Lucknow.
3. The District Entertaiment Tax Officer,
Office of District Magistrate Entertainment Tax
Section, Haridwar.
4. Upper Mukhya Adhikari, Zila Parishad, Haridwar. - Respondents
(2) Writ Petition No. 1030 (M/S) of 2007
(Old No. 83 of 1994)

Usha Breco Limited, Upper Road, Haridwar,
 through its Resident Manager, Sri R.A. Sharma - Petitioner
 Versus
 1- Commissioner of Entertainment Tax, U.P.
 Lucknow.
 2- District Magistrate/Collector Haridwar.
 3- Additional District Magistrate (Entertainment

 4- Additional District Magistrate (Finance and Revenue)
 Haridwar.
 5- Tehsildar, Sadar, Haridwar - Respondents
(3) Writ Petition No. 1032 (M/S) of 2007
 (Old No. 1376/1997)
 1- Usha Breco Limited, Chandi Devi Rope Way,
 Near Gauri Shankar Temple, Hardwar,
 through its Divisional Manager, Sri M.J. Raghuram,
 2- Sri K.P. Pandey S/o Sri Ram Kishore Pandey,
 R/o Haridwar, a shareholder of Usha Breco Ltd. - Petitioners
 Versus
 1- State of U.P. through its Chief Secretary,
State Secretariat, Vidhan Sabha Marg, Lucknow.

2
2- Commissioner of Entertainment Tax, U.P.
Jawahar Bhawan, Ashok Road, Lucknow.
3- The Additional Commissioner,
Entertainment Tax, U.P. Jawahar Bhawan
Ashoka Road, Lucknow.
4- The District Entertaiment Tax Officer,
Office of District Magistrate Entertainment Tax
Section, Haridwar.
5- Executive Commissioner,
Haridwar Municipal Board,
Haridwar - Respondents
Sri Navneet Kaushik, Advocate for the petitioners.
Sri A.S. Rawat, Additional Advocate General along with Mr. I.P. Kohli,
Standing Counsel on behalf of State/respondent.
Sri Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the Nagar Palika Haridwar
[Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. )
 Since similar controversy is involved in the above noted three
writ petitions, therefore, all the writ petitions were heard together and
are being decided by this common judgment.
 In Writ Petition No. 1031(M/S) 2007, the petitioner has sought
a writ in nature of certiorari for quashing the letter dated 17th
February, 1997, Annexure No. IV to the writ petition, by which the
District Entertainment Tax Officer, Office of District Magistrate
Entertainment Tax Section, Haridwar has directed the petitioner to
pay entertainment tax @ 30% of the passenger fare charged by the
petitioner Usha Breco Limited.
In Writ Petition No. 1032 (M/S) of 2007, the petitioner has
sought a writ in the nature of certiorari for quashing the Officer Order
dated 28-2-1997, Annexure No. I to the writ petition, by which the
Commissioner of Entertainment Tax, U.P. Lucknow, has directed the
petitioner to pay entertainment tax.
 In the above two writ petitions, direction is also sought to
declare Section 2(g) of U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax, as ultra
vires, so far as it is applicable to the aerial ropeways being run by the
petitioners.
 In Writ Petition No. 1030 (M/S) of 2007, writ in the nature of
certiorari has been sought to quash the order dated 13.1.1994,
Annexure No.5 to the writ petition, by which the Additional District

3
Magistrate, (Finance) Haridwar, imposed entertainment tax upon the
petitioner.
 By way of amendment sought through CLMA No. 8009/2012
filed in Writ Petition No. 1031(M/S) of 2007, the prayer was sought
to issue a writ in the nature of certiorari for quashing the notification
No.58/2010/XXVII(9)/Mano.kar-28/2009 dated 6-9-2010, so far as it
relates to imposition of entertainment tax on ropeway at the rate of
20% of each payment for admission.
 Brief facts giving rise to the present writ petitions, are that the
petitioner Usha Breco Limited, is engaged in the business of
designing, supplying, civil engineering, erection, commissioning,
maintaining and operation of the aerial passenger ropeways. The
petitioner Sri Ram Kishore Pandey is a shareholder of the petitioner
company. In order to provide transportation of passengers for easy
and comfortable access to Chandi Devi Temple and Goddess Mansa
Devi Temple, the petitioner entered into an agreement with the Zila
Parishad Haridwar and Municipal Board Haridwar for operating
aerial ropeways for the sole purpose of carriage of passengers. As per
agreements, the petitioner installed ropeways from the lower
terminal adjacent to Gauri Shanker Temple to upper terminal adjacent
to the Chandi Devi Temple and from lower terminal station situated
in the leased land to upper terminal station situated in the leased lands
near Mansa Devi Temple.
 It is alleged by the petitioner that the ropeways are established
by the petitioner only to facilitate the transportation of the pilgrims for
a visit to Mansa Devi and to Chandi Devi Temples. The pilgrims after
having Darshan of the above Temples board the ropeways to return
to the lower terminals. There is no question of entertainment for the
pilgrims for having Darshan of the religious temples of Mansa Devi
and Chandi Devi and the sole purpose of their visit to the hill top is
the pilgrimage and there is no source of entertainment for them at the
hill top. It is also alleged by the petitioner that as per provision of
Section 2(g) of the U.P. Entertainment and Betting Act, 1979 (for
short 'the Act') 'entertainment' includes any exhibition,
performance, amusement, game, sport or race (including horse race)
to which persons are admitted for payment and in the case of

4
cinematograph exhibitions, includes exhibition of news-reels,
documentaries, cartoons, advertisement shorts or slides, whether
before or during the exhibition of a feature film or separately.
Although the power to make laws for ropeways is with the State
Government under Entry No.13 List-II, but there is no specific power
with the State Government to levy taxes on the carriage of passengers
by ropeways as compared to the specific power to levy tax on
entertainment, amusement etc. The power of the State Government to
levy tax on goods and passengers is limited to only those who are
carried or transported by road or on inland water-ways. The carriage
of passengers by aerial ropeways cannot be said to be carriage by road
or on inland water-ways. The carriage/transportation of passengers by
aerial ropeways is a means of aerial transport and, as such, the power
to levy tax on such carriage would be with the Union Government in
view of Entry 89 List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. It
is also alleged by the petitioner that the petitioner was to pay lease
rent and consumption of electricity, house tax and water tax. But
surprisingly enough the respondents issued impugned notices/office
orders asking the petitioner to deposit entertainment tax, whereas the
main and predominate use of the ropeways is transportation and
nothing else and as such the running of ropeways canot be termed as
providing entertainment to the passengers so as to bring the ropeways
within the ambit of Act and the demand of entertainment tax is illegal
and is liable to be quashed.
 The writ petitions have been resisted by the respondents by
filing counter affidavits. The stand taken by respondents is that the
first ropeway was introduced in the State in Mussoorie and
subsequently at Nainital, the objective behind providing the ropeway
was to save time and physical exercise involved in reaching the hill
top and also to provide ample visibility of the sight all around.
Thereafter the ropeways in question came into existence. The
petitioner is a commercial organization. According to the agreement
between the petitioner and Nagar Palika Parishad dated 15-5-1974
ropeway was erected for purpose of business. There had been a
proposal between the petitioner and Nagar Palika Parishad for
installing a plant and equipment for the transportation by cabin ride

5
aerial ropeway of passengers from Brahmapuro to Mayapur Block, the
name of Mansa Devi is mentioned. Under the agreement the petitioner
was to run cafeteria, snack bar and amusement center for
entertainment of the passengers, inter alia in transit building at the
upper terminal station of the said cabin ride aerial ropeway. The
representatives of petitioner have accepted that the people using cabin
ride feel thrill and enjoyment in natural way. It is further alleged in
the written statement that ropeway cabin ride comes under the
purview of 'entertainment' as envisaged under U.P. Entertainment &
Betting Tax Act, 1979. It is also alleged that the passengers are
always taxable uniformally whether on the hills or on a hill top or
even in any place of pilgrimage therefore the levy of tax is neither
ultra vires nor arbitrary, nor illegal nor violative of Article 19(i)(G),
245, 265, 300-A because the U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax Act
to the extent defined is enforceable and entertainment tax having been
imposed by authority of law, can never amount to deprival of property
as has been alleged. It is totally wrong to allege that the instant cases
fall within the provision of entry 89 of List-1 pertaining to terminal
taxes on goods and passengers carried by Railway, Sea or Air Or
Railway fares and freights, because the ropeway cabin is never
comparable to an aeroplane. Entry 33 of List-II of the VIIth Schedule
deals with theatre and dramatic performance cinemas, sports,
entertainments and amusements and because the instant case of
employing the ropeways for resort and entertainment equally amounts
to amusement taxable under the said Act, 1979.
 Petitioner also filed rejoinder affidavits and reiterated that the
ropeways are being run for transportation of passengers for the
Darshan of the temples and no entertainment tax is liable to be levied
on the petitioner.
 In Writ Petition No. 1031 (M/S) 2007, this court on 24-7-2009,
had directed the petitioner to file supplementary affidavit giving
details and clarifying the facts mentioned in the petition as well as in
the affidavit within four weeks and State was also directed to file
additional counter affidavit explaining the paragraphs which are vague
and submit the documents.

6
 In compliance of order of this court the petitioner filed
supplementary affidavit and in para-7 it has been alleged that there is
no activity of entertainment and/or amusement at the terminal station
or for entry of which, any charge is made by the petitioners in the fare.
Petitioners have only small temporary kiosks/counters provided for at
the lower station and the terminal station, which are let out to different
vendors, who sell different products for consideration. It has been
alleged that five kiosks/counters are running at lower station and 13
small counters/kiosks are at the upper station, details of which has
been given in the supplementary counter affidavit. It is further alleged
that none of the activities or goods at the shops are given or offered to
the passengers free of costs or are charged in the ropeway fare. There
is also no compulsion on any one to buy goods provided at the said
establishments and/ or to pay any charges, unless the passengers so
require. The entire fare charged by the petitioners at the ropeway is
entirely for purpose of transporting passengers from one point to other
and there is no element of entertainment or amusement and/or any
other activity provided to the passengers, which is included in the
fare. The learned Commissioner has failed to appreciate that for the
purpose of determining whether the activities of transportation of
passengers amount to entertainment or not, the test has to be objective
test, i.e. nature of service/goods provided and received and no
subjective test, which has been applied by Commissioner. Merely
because, some people may get pleasure in travelling by ropeways,
will not change the objective of the payment made for travelling
thereon.
 In reply to supplementary affidavit, the State filed
supplementary counter affidavit and reiterated the facts narrated in the
writ petition. It has been alleged in the supplementary counter
affidavit that clause 2(g) of U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax Act,
1979, is legally competent to define ropeway run by petitioner as
Entertainment or Equipment of providing Entertainment/Amusement.
The ropeway run by the petitioner falls in the ambit of entertainment
tax under Section 3(1) of the Act. The Constitutional provisions of the
rights and power to make Act and Rules relating to the entertainment
firmly explain that State of Uttarakhand has absolute power in State

7
List of Constitution and State of Uttarakhand has issued G.O. No.
58/2010/XXV11(9)Mano. Kar-28/2009 Dated 6-9-2010. In the
Schedule 5(b) it is clearly indicated that 20% of admission fee is liable
as entertainment tax on ropeway including other entertainments.
Copy of aforesaid G.O. has been annexed as Annexure No.SCA-1.
 After the amendment in the writ petition No. 1031 (M/S) 2007,
the petitioner also sought quashing of Notification dated 6-9-2010 so
far as it relates to imposition of entertainment tax on rope-way, the
respondent has filed reply by filing supplementary counter affidavit.
In the supplementary counter affidavit the stand taken in the counter
affidavit has been reiterated. It is further alleged in the supplementary
counter affidavit that the definition of entertainment as contained
under Section 2(g) of the U.P. Entertainments and Betting Tax Act,
1979 is an inclusive definition and not exhaustive and a thing which is
not necessary is an entertainment, consequently, the ropeway is an
entertainment within the ambit of Section 2(g) of the Tax Act. In para-5 of the supplementary counter affidavit it has been alleged that the
prayer for declaring the Section 2 (g) of the U.P. Entertainment and
Betting Tax Act ulta vires is wholly misconceived as it is well settled
that the vires of an Act can be challenged only on two grounds
namely-(a) lack of competent and (b) violation of any of the provision
of the Constitution of India including part III of it, but the petitioner
has not shown as to how the State Legislature has no competent to
enact the said provision which has been made in exercise of powers
conferred under Article 246(3) of the Constitution of India nor the
same in any manner violates any provisions of the Constitution of
Indian much less a provision conferred under Part-III of the
Constitution of India.
 In para-6 of the supplementary counter affidavit it is pleaded
that against the order dated 28-11-1996 passed by Hon'ble Allahabad
High Court in writ petition No. 373 of 1996 filed by the petitioner
itself has remitted the matter with a direction to Commissioner to
decide afresh within a period of three months against the petitioner
preferred a Special Leave Petition and the same was dismissed as
withdrawn.

8
 In para-7 of the supplementary counter affidavit, it has been
alleged that the Apex Court has not touched the finding of Division
Bench of Allahabad High court and since the order dated 17-2-1997
has been passed in compliance of the judgment of Allahabad High
Court, it is not open for the petitioner to challenge the vires of the Act
or its application as the said issue stand concluded under the judgment
of the Allahabad High Court wherein also the challenge was made to
the Tax Act, but the same are deemed to be repelled by the Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court and even the Apex Court has not
made it open for the petitioner to re-agitate the matter regarding the
validity of the Act or its application.
 It is further alleged in para-9 of the supplementary counter
affidavit that the notification dated 9-6-2010 issued in exercise of
powers conferred under the Tax Act read with section 21 of the U.P.
General Clauses Act is well within the competence of the State
Government and the petitioner who is providing an entertainment has
no option, but to deposit the entertainment tax.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
 The relief sought by the petitioner is to the effect that the
entertainment tax imposed by the respondents be set aside and
declaration be made that provisions of U.P. Entertainment and Betting
Tax Act, 1979 are not applicable to the petitioner Company on
carriage of passengers by aerial ropeways to Chandi Devi Temple and
Mansa Devi Temple. By amendment further relief has been sought
that the notification dated 6-9-2010 be quashed so far as it relates to
imposition of entertainment tax on rope way under the U.P.
Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979.
 The main question to be decided in these writ petitions is
whether the petitioner Company is liable to pay entertainment tax on
carriage of passengers by aerial ropeways to Chandi Temple and
Mansa Temple under the U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax Act,
1979, or not and the State Government has the competence to issue
notification imposing entertainment tax on rope way.
 The submission raised on behalf of the petitioners, is that
ropeways are statutorily recognized as means of transportation and is
excluded from entertainment tax and the Petitioner Company cannot

9
be held liable to pay entertainment tax on the ropeways under the U.P.
Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979.
 On the other hand, the submission of learned Addl. Advocate
General is that the ropeways are used for the convenience of tourists,
and the passengers feel thrill and enjoyment in natural way and the
use of ropeways comes in the purview of 'entertainment' as envisaged
under U.P. Entertainment & Betting Tax Act, 1979.
 To decide the controversy certain provisions U.P. Entertainment
and Belting Tax Act 1979 and Constitution of India need to be
examined.
 Word 'Entertainment' is defined in Section 2(g) of the U.P.
Entertainment Betting Tax Act, 1979, which reads as under:-
'entertainment' includes any exhibition, performance, amusement,
game, sport, or race (including horse race) to which persons are
admitted for payment and in the case of cinematographic
exhibitions, includes the exhibition of news reels, documentaries,
cartoons, advertisement shots, or slides, whether before or during
the exhibition of a feature film or separately.'
 From a plain reading of above, it is quite obvious that
transportation of passengers by ropeways is not included in the
'entertainment', only word 'amusement' is included, and by using
the ropeways to the holy temples of Chandi and Mansa Devi, cannot
be termed an amusement. The pilgrims visit these temples for
Darshan having religious spirit. There is no place of enjoyment in
between the ropeways and at the site of Temples there are shops
having articles of puja and charawa. There might be some
restaurant for tea, snack etc. but the same cannot be termed as
means of amusement and enjoyment.
 Entry 13 of List II of Schedule-7 of Constitution of India
recognizes ropeways as a means of communications and confers
legislative competence on the States to enact laws regulating such
activity. Entry 13 reads as under:
 '13. Communications, that is to say, roads, bridges, ferries and
other means of communication not specified in List I; municipal
tramways; ropeways; inland waterways and traffic thereon subject

10
to the provisions of List I and List III with regard to such
waterways; vehicles other than mechanically propelled vehicles.'
 From above, it is quite clear that the ropeway comes within the
purview of communications, as per entry 13 above.
 The U.P. Entertainment and Tax Act 1979 has been enacted
consequent to the legislative power conferred on the State by Entry 62
of List-II, which reads as under:-
 '62. Taxes on luxuries, including taxes on entertainments,
amusements, betting and gambling.'
 The tax charging section of the said Act reads as under:-
'Tax on payment for admission to entertainment:(1) Subject to the
provisions of this Act, there shall be levied and paid on all payments
for admission to any entertainment, other than on entertainment to
which Section 4 or Section 4-A applies or a compounded payment is
made under the proviso to this sub-section, an entertainment tax at
such rate not exceeding one hundred and fifty percent of each such
payment as the Statement Government may from time to time notify
in this behalf, and the tax shall be collected by the proprietor from
the person making the payment for admission and paid to the
Government in the manner prescribed.'
Further entry 56 provides taxes on goods and passengers carried
by road or on inland waterways and entry 57 provides taxes on
vehicles, whether mechanically propelled or not, suitable for use on
roads, including tramcars subject to the provisions of entry 35 of List
III.
 The taxes on goods and passengers carried by road or on
waterways under entry 56 and also taxes on vehicles under 57 are
compensatory taxes designed to compensate Government for the
expenses incurred in maintaining public roadways and public
waterways. As against this Government does not incur any
expenditure, in relation to ropeways, and there is absence of any
entry conferring power on the State to levy taxes on ropeways. The
State can levy entertainment tax on under the head of 'amusement'
contained in the definition of 'entertainment' under Section 2(g) of
U.P. Entertainment and Betting Act, 1979. As per entry 13 of List II
of Schedule-7 of Constitution of India, ropeway has been placed as

11
means of communication. The competence of State government is to
impose tax on the ropeways under the head of 'communication' and
not under the head 'amusement' as has been done in the instant case.
 The learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance upon
the judgment of Commissioner of Central excise Pondicherry versus
Acer India Ltd. reported in (2004) 8 Supreme Court Cases 173,
wherein it has been observed by the Apex Court that while levying
excise duty an interpretation leading to wide-scale evasion of duty,
should be avoided and a user-friendly interpretation should be
adopted.
 In another case of M/s Geeta Enterprises and others vs. State of
U.P. and others, reported in AIR 1983 Supreme Court 1098, the
issue before the Apex Court was whether video show is exigible to
tax under Section 3 of U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax Act. It
has been observed by the Apex Court as under:-
 'The word 'entertainment' has been used in S. 2(3) in a very wide
sense so as to include within its ambit, entertainment of any kind
including one which may be purely educative. Sub-section (3) itself
by using the word 'entertainment' as 'any exhibitional performance,
amusement game or sport to which persons are admitted for
payment' has extended the scope of entertainment to expressly
include any kind of amusement, game or sport. By operating the
video, the operator of the video pays 50 paise per 30 seconds for
playing the games, sports and other kind of performance which are
shown on the machine and which can be watched by interested
spectators. The circumstance that no admission fee is charged from
viewers of video by itself, however, cannot defuse or alter the kind of
entertainment derived by the person who pays for playing the
games. The fact that for playing the video games a great amount of
skill is required is not material because he would derive pleasure
and be entertained regardless of whether he possesses skill or not. If
he possesses skill he may derive more pleasure on less payment
otherwise he will have to pay but he will derive pleasure all the
same. Besides, the game brings a substantial return for the person
who makes available these facilities. Hence such an exhibition falls
within the purview of the word entertainment as envisaged in sub-

12
section (3). The money charged for use of the video machine is an
admission to entertainment and the payment made by the person
who uses the machine is the payment for admission. It is a payment
connected with entertainment, which a person is required to make as
a condition of attending the entertainment. Hence as video show is
clearly exigible to tax under Section 3 of the Act."
 It has further been observed that the crux of the matter is as to
whether or not the show falls within the four corners of the
expression 'entertainment'. Sub section (3) of Section 2 of the Act
defines the 'entertainment' which includes any exhibitional
performance, amusement, game or sport to which persons are
admitted for payment.
 The word 'entertainment' has been defined in Webster's Third
New International dictionary at page 757 as -
 'entertainment' the act of diverting, amusing, or causing someone's
time to pass agreeably.'
'Something that diverts, amuses, or occupies the attention
agreeably.'
Similarly in the Concise English Dictionary by Hayward and
Sparkes the word 'entertainment' has been defined as-
'the art of entertainment, amusing or diverting, the pleasure
afforded to the mind by anything interesting, amusement, other
performance indented to amuse.'
Thus in wider sense the word 'entertainment' can be taken
amusement, any act which may afford pleasure to the mind or
occupies one's attention towards anything interesting.
 It has been contended on behalf of State that the Apex Court
has not touched the finding of Division Bench of Allahabad High
court and since the order dated 17-2-1997 has been passed in
compliance of the judgment of Allahabad High Court, it is not open
for the petitioner to challenge the vires of the Act or its application
as the said issue stand concluded under the judgment of the
Allahabad High Court wherein also the challenge was made to the
Tax Act, but the same are deemed to be repelled by the Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court and even the Apex Court has not

13
made it open for the petitioner to re-agitate the matter regarding the
validity of the Act or its application.
 By a perusal of order dated 28-11-1996 passed by Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court in W.P. No. 37 of 1996, it shows
that District Magistrate Haridwar issued an order dated 15.12.1992
directing the petitioner to deposit the entertainment tax at the rate
prescribed. The petitioner filed objection against the said notice.
Another notice dated 12.2.1993 was issued to the petitioner asking it
to deposit the entertainment tax for the period from July 1993 to
November, 1993. Against the said notice petitioner filed W.P. No.
635(T) of 1993 before Allahabad High Court in which stay order
was granted to the petitioner. Another order dated 13.2.1994 was
issued by A.D.M. Haridwar asking the petitioner to deposit the
amount. Against the said order petitioner filed another W.P. No. 83
of 1994 in which matter interim order was granted. Writ Petition No.
635 of 1993 was disposed of on 10-7-1995 directing the concerned
authority to deal with the matter afresh. Thereafter notice dated 30-
10-1995 was given to the petitioner calling upon it to submit its
reply. The petitioner submitted its reply and Commissioner of
Entertainment Tax U.P. passed order dated 2.4.1996 holding the
petitioner liable to pay the entertainment tax under the Act. Feeling
aggrieved the petitioner filed W.P. No. 373 of 1996. In the above
writ petition the Division Bench of Allahabad High Court directed
the Commissioner to decide the matter afresh after spot
inspection/survey in the presence of authorized representative of
petitioner. Against above order Special Leave to Appeal (Civil) No.
1675 of 1997 was preferred before the Apex Court and the Apex
Court vide order dated2-5-1997 dismissed the SLP as withdrawn.
The order passed by Apex Court is quoted below:-
 'We have not gone into the merits of the questions raised because
the consequential order passed pursuant to the order of the High
Court has been challenged in the High Court itself. The Special
Leave Petition is dismissed as withdrawn.'
 The Additional Entertainment Tax Commissioner in
compliance of order of the High Court dated 28-11-1996 after
inquiry again issued notices to the petitioner to deposit the tax

14
against which the present writ petitions are filed. From above, it is
quite clear that the Division Bench of Allahabad High Court had
passed interim order in favour of the petitioner and has directed the
Commissioner to decide the matter afresh at its level. In the order of
Allahabad High Court there is no direction which may not permit
the petitioner to agitate the matter. The issue whether the petitioner
is liable to pay entertainment or not has not yet been decided and
the issue has to be decided in the present writ petitions. So far as
the order passed by Hon'ble Apex Court is concerned has dismissed
the S.L.P. without entering in the merits of the question on the
ground the question has been challenged in the High Court. Thus the
submission of the State Counsel is of no avail that the petitioner
cannot re-agitate the matter on the basis of orders passed by High
Court and the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
 In view of discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs, the
State has competence in view of Entry-13 of List-II of Schedule-7
of Constitution of India which recognizes ropeways as a means of
communications and confers legislative competence on the States to
enact laws regulating such activity. The United Provinces Aerial
Ropeways Act, 1922 is in force in State of Uttarakhand also as it
was in force in the State of U.P. by the enactment. Amendment if
any could be made for imposing any type of tax under that Act. As
on today the said Act does not contain provision to impose the
entertainment tax on ropeways. The power under U.P.
Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979 was enacted consequent to
the Legislative powers conferred on the State by Entry 62 of List -II
of Schedule-7 of Constitution of India. The learned Entertainment
Commissioner has imposed the entertainment tax considering the
ride of rope-ways as an amusement. The finding of learned
Commissioner on this issue is totally perverse finding and the State
Government instead of making amendment in the United Provinces
Aerial Ropeways Act, 1922, issued the impugned notification in
exercise of power under the U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax
Act, 1979 and added sub-clause (b) in clause-5 of impugned
notification dated 6-9-2010, making a provision of 20% tax of each
payment for admission over rope-ways. This notification dated 6-9-

15
2010, was issued without legislative competence under the U.P.
Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979, and in any view of the
matter, as discussed above, on the rope-way cannot be said to be
amusement under the U.P. Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979.
 Thus, for the discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs, it is
quite clear that the State Government has no competence to impose
entertainment tax on the ropeways installed at Chandi Devi and
Mansa Devi Temples under the provision of Section 2 (g) of U.P.
Entertainment and Betting Tax Act, 1979 and the Notification dated
6-9-2010, so far as making provision of 20% tax of each payment
for admission over ropeway, under sub clause (b) of clause 5 has
been issued without legislative competence. Therefore, the
Notification No. 58/2010/XXVII(9)/ Mano.kar-28/2009, dated 6th
September, 2010, is quashed in respect of sub-clause (b) of clause-5
and rope way is treated to be deleted from the said Notification as no
tax under the head 'entertainment' is payable on ropeway.
 Consequently, the letter dated 17th February, 1997, Annexure
No. IV to the W.P. No. 1031(M/S) 2007 issued by District
Entertainment Tax Section, Haridwar; the Office Order dated 28-2-
1997, Annexure No.1 to W.P. No. 1032(M/S) of 2007 issued by
Commissioner of Entertainment Tax, U.P. Lucknow; and the order
dated 13.1.1994, Annexure No.5 to the W.P. No. 1030(M/S) 2007

It is pertinent to mention here that the Allahabad High Court in writ
petition Nos. 635(T)/1993, 83(T)/1994 and 373 (T)/1996 vide order
dated 28-11-1996 gave directions to decide the issue as per rules
within three months. In compliance of above direction, Additional
Entertainment Commissioner was appointed as enquiry officers and
the Commissioner Entertainment Tax Department issued direction to
petitioner vide impugned order dated 28-2-1997 to deposit the entire
balance amount of entertainment tax deposited in the government
treasury and in future entertainment tax be regularly deposited in
government treasury. In the impugned order it was held that
subsequent to giving the land on lease domain of the Municipality is
limited but due to these facts that there being no objection regarding
cafeteria, restaurant in the agreement and making the arrangements
generally for establishing the ropeways and these arrangements being
especially for the tourists and the ropeway being mostly used by the
tourists since objective of the visitors is to go by walk which they
believe is the healthiest, holy and meaningful and the use of the
ropeway is with the objectives of entertainment and amusement
alongwith earning of profit in the form of a commercial establishment,
hence the entertainment tax is liable to be paid.
Further in writ petition No. 1148 of 2003
(M/B) Usha Breco Ltd. versus State of U.P. and others, the Division
Bench of this Court while disposing of the Civil Misc. Application
No. 5256 of 2004, moved by petitioner to cancel the attachment of its
properties in lieu of recovery of entertainment tax, vide order dated
16-9-2004, cancelled the attachment and directed to return back the
amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- recovered as a condition to continue the
ropeway and all the proceedings initiated for the recovery of the
amount of 50% was treated to be cancelled and the stay order already
granted to directed to continue.
